svg.title: Evidence and claim boundary for the technology skill renewal study
svg.desc: Visual separates observed O*NET database evidence, defensible L&D interpretation, and claims the study does not make.
svg.text: Evidence Boundary: What the Study Shows — and What It Does Not
Separating measured database turnover from workforce-planning interpretation

g.text: Common-code pair Jaccard: 0.7016 across 902 common occupations
Category-name sensitivity: 0.8169 · broader categories persist more strongly
Use the signal to prioritize where technology requirements appear more stable versus more renewal-heavy.
Use exact-name and category-level results together when discussing reskilling, curriculum refresh, and workforce planning.
No causal rate of human skill depreciation · no worker performance loss · no training effectiveness estimate
Observed turnover can also reflect taxonomy maintenance, content updates, vendor naming, or database revisions.
